identity.name: Paprika extract (capsanthin, capsorubin)
identity.chemical_class: Natural carotenoid (xanthophyll) extract from Capsicum annuum

function.mechanism: Carotenoid pigments (mainly capsanthin/capsorubin) absorb shorter wavelengths and impart red-orange colour to foods.

adi.basis: EFSA ADI for paprika extract; EFSA also reported 1.7 mg carotenoids/kg bw/day equivalent

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no genotoxic concern and no carcinogenicity at tested doses; refined exposure scenarios were below ADI.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR 73.345 (Paprika oleoresin); 21 CFR 73.340 (Paprika); 21 CFR 182.20 (GRAS listing for paprika/capsicum natural extractives)

adi.basis: JECFA ADI is 0-1.5 mg/kg bw (paprika extract, as total carotenoids basis in record)

concerns.summary: A 2025 cohort study reported higher type 2 diabetes incidence with certain additive mixtures that included paprika extract; signal is mixture-level and observational, not causal for E160c alone.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA: no genotoxic concern and no carcinogenicity at tested doses in re-evaluation.
JECFA: dietary exposure estimate below ADI and no health concern at assessed intake.
90-day rat study reported NOAEL > 2000 mg/kg bw/day for capsanthin-rich extract.
12-week human supplementation study reported no adverse events at 20 or 100 mg/day paprika oleoresin.

adi_exceedance.notes: JECFA estimated high-percentile intake at 0.1-0.2 mg/kg bw/day (below ADI 0-1.5 mg/kg bw/day); EFSA reported refined scenarios below ADI.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory assessments are consistently favorable with established ADIs and exposure estimates generally below those ADIs; residual uncertainty mainly concerns additive-mixture epidemiology and extract heterogeneity rather than a strong direct hazard signal.
key_factors: EFSA ADI established with no genotoxic/carcinogenic concern in core data
JECFA ADI and intake estimates indicate no health concern at assessed exposure
FDA color-additive approvals with GMP restrictions and certification exemption
No IARC classification found for paprika extract
Recent observational mixture study is non-causal and not specific to E160c alone
